Aggregate income: No data are available. Values are assigned using a regional average or another assumed value solely to ensure coverage. This is the lowest-quality category and is used only as a last resort.
Aggregate wealth: No data are available. Values are assigned using a regional average to ensure coverage. This is the lowest-quality category and is used only as a last resort.
Indices & Exchange Rates: No data are available; a static value is assumed. This is the lowest-quality category and is used only as a last resort to ensure coverage.
Population: No observation is classified with this score.

Aggregate income: Values are estimated by extrapolating nearby observations using simple assumptions, such as forward/backward projection, moving averages, regional growth rates, or stable relationships with a related country or former common jurisdiction.
Aggregate wealth: Values are estimated by extrapolating nearby OLS predictions with regional average.
Indices & Exchange Rates: The value is imputed either directly or by projecting an observation using a secondary variable -or the same variable- as a reference for growth observed in one or more neighbouring countries (or countries with historical affiliations) (e.g., imputation of exchange rates based on comparisons of Yugoslav GDP values expressed in different currency terms, with the resulting estimates applied to the former Yugoslav countries).
Population: The value is imputed by projecting the nearest available observation forward or backward, assuming constant relative shares, estimated in a recent reference period, between the country and the aggregate of another country with which it was part of the same jurisdiction at some point in time (e.g. the Czech Republic and Slovakia following the dissolution of Czechoslovakia).

Aggregate income: Values are estimated using statistical or econometric methods, such as OLS regressions on relevant macroeconomic covariates or signal-extraction techniques (e.g., Hodrick–Prescott filtering).
Aggregate wealth: Values are estimated using OLS regressions on relevant macroeconomic country-specific covariates rather than past observations.
Indices & Exchange Rates: The value is imputed by projecting an observation using a secondary variable observed within the same country as a reference (e.g., KP PPP exchange rate calculated based on the comparison of GDP values expressed in different currency terms), or by carrying the nearest available observation forward or backward.
Population: The value is imputed by projecting the nearest available observation forward or backward, using growth rates or age shares observed in the country’s available totals.

Aggregate income: Values are estimated by linear interpolation between observed data points or derived through the simultaneous adjustment of macroeconomic identities to ensure internal consistency.
Aggregate wealth: Values are estimated by extending nearby directly observed data with regional average.
Indices & Exchange Rates: Values are estimated by linear interpolation between two known data points, filling short internal gaps.
Population: Values are estimated using linear interpolation between adjacent data points to fill short internal gaps.

Aggregate income: Values are directly sourced from older national accounting frameworks, benchmark academic studies, or historical compilations. Comparability with current standards may be limited.
Aggregate wealth: Values are estimated by extending nearby directly observed data with OLS predictions.
Indices & Exchange Rates: Values are sourced from benchmark academic research, historical compilations, forecasts under the latest SNA (e.g., IMF WEO estimates of deflators for some countries in the past year), or from older SNA frameworks.
Population: Values are directly sourced from historical compilations; comparability with current standards may be limited.

Aggregate income: Values are directly observed from the most recent national accounts compiled under the latest SNA standards. This is the highest-quality category.
Aggregate wealth: Values are directly observed in official balance sheets (from the most recent national accounts compiled under the latest SNA standards), global asset datasets, or validated academic studies. This is the highest-quality category.
Indices & Exchange Rates: Values are directly observed from the most recent national accounts under the latest SNA, representing the highest-quality data.
Population: Values are directly observed from the UN World Population Prospects or from the most recent national accounts compiled under the latest SNA, representing the highest-quality data.
